title.narrative: ROAS/LEB/Reducing Marine Litter in the Mediterranean through Waste Wise Cities Lebanon (ReMaL)

description.narrative:
ReMaL aims to reduce marine litter by supporting coastal Lebanese UoMs and the national government in establishing the foundations of ISWM through the following approach:
• Work Package (WP) 1 Preparation (Output I): This WP will be the starting point of the project and establish the foundations for the future work, such as a joint understanding of the collaboration between all partners. To be able to communicate on the project progress and results, as well as share knowledge, a National Online Waste Observatory (NOWO) will be established through consultations with the Ministry of Environment (MoE), led by UN-Habitat (UNH). Moreover, the observatory's design will be developed by the Wuppertal Institut für Klima, Umwelt, Energie gGmbH (also known as Wuppertal Institute for Climate, Environment and Energy [WI]). To prepare for the baseline assessment and subsequent planning of the ISWM systems, the collaboration with the UoMs will be defined together with the whole project team. A survey on the available UoMs' data on solid waste, its status and any relevant background information and data (e.g. population data) will be conducted by the whole project team. The plastic recovery capacity of the targeted UoMs and at the national level will also be mapped, mainly through UNH. To raise awareness for the project and put it on the agenda of participating UoMs and the political partners (national ministries) a kick-off event will be organized by UNH, supported by WI, back-to-back with a training on the Waste Wise Cities Tool (WaCT) for officials of the targeted UoMs.
• WP2 Identification of Interventions (Output I): Based on the outputs of WP1, this work package will identify, in a participatory process, the intervention areas through an analysis of policy and infrastructure gaps, as well as the activities to close these gaps. Therefore, the UoMs will be supported by UNH in implementing the WaCT and analysis of the collected data to establish a baseline on solid waste. Furthermore, the UoMs will be guided by UNH on additional observations for plastic leakage which enables them to develop Waste Flow Diagrams (WFDs) for each UoM. Based on the results from the WaCT and WFDs, the project team will identify main intervention areas and infrastructure gaps in coordination with the UoMs. The results of the baseline assessment (WaCT and WFD), as well as the identified intervention areas and gaps will then be presented in a first series of stakeholder workshops, one in each participating UoM, organized by UNH and prepared by the project team. During the workshop the participating stakeholders will validate the findings and brainstorm on possible solutions. Based on the results from the workshops, the project team will then support the municipality officials in selecting the intervention options that can be considered as “fast win” pilot projects, as well as promising larger infrastructure measures. These will address current barriers to successful ISWM (such as sorting at source, efficient collection, awareness raising, etc.) and then turned into project proposals by the UoMs with support from the project team. Furthermore, the UoMs will be encouraged to draft Solid Waste Management (SWM) and Marine Litter Prevention Action Plans.
• WP3 Pilot Projects (Output II): Based on the project proposals developed in WP2, the pilot projects will be implemented in collaboration with the UoMs and local partners. The project proposals that have been developed based on the results of the first participatory workshop series (under WP2), will be presented, discussed and improved in a second series of workshops organized by UNH, supported by WI, in each participating UoM. Again, all stakeholders need to be invited and included. The second series of workshops will be communicated as a continuation of the work and discussions of WP2. The project proposals will be finalized by the project team and the UoMs based on the feedback of the stakeholders received during the workshop, as well as in writing after the events. If necessary, calls with selected stakeholders will be organized to clarify important points. Based on the project proposals the pilot projects will be planned by the project team together with the relevant UoMs and local partners. The local partners will be identified and sub-contracted by UNH through a competitive selection process following UN-Habitat’s Implementing Partner Policy. For the project planning and implementation, it will be important to liaise with relevant stakeholders, for which UNH will be planning and conducting meetings. Once the concepts for the pilot projects are defined, the project team will support the UoMs and local partners in the implementation of the selected projects. Special care will be taken to include scavengers and vulnerable groups in the implementation.
